# R2R Labs

Risk limits, a kill switch and an audit log for AI agents trading Hyperliquid
perpetuals. The limits are enforced outside the model, in a process it cannot
reach, so they hold whatever the agent decides or is told to do.

## Pages

- https://r2rlabs.com/ — what Reins is, what it refuses, and the demo run's numbers.
- https://r2rlabs.com/mcp/ — the Hyperliquid MCP server: connecting Claude, Claude
  Code or Cursor, the tools a model gets, and the rules that refuse it.
- https://r2rlabs.com/cloud/ — Reins Cloud, the hosted version being built: human
  approval on large orders, a kill switch only an owner resets, alerts by email,
  Telegram and SMS, and what has and has not run so far.
- https://r2rlabs.com/build/ — contract work: the person who built Reins is
  available to build the same kind of thing for you.

## Facts

- Reins is free and open source (MIT): https://github.com/R2Rlabs/reins
- Install: npx @r2rlabs/reins init — https://www.npmjs.com/package/@r2rlabs/reins
- From Python: pip install reins-client — https://pypi.org/project/reins-client/
  (no dependencies; the same limits over HTTP, refusals raised with their code)
- Listed in the MCP Registry as io.github.R2Rlabs/hyperliquid-reins
- Paper trading is free and needs no key: simulated fills on live prices, same limits.
- Live trading pays 2 basis points of the volume it protects, as a Hyperliquid
  builder fee. There is no subscription.
- An agent signs with a Hyperliquid API wallet, which can trade but cannot withdraw.
- Reins Cloud is in development and not open for sign-ups. It has traded on
  Hyperliquid testnet, signed by a fallback vault; the production key custody is
  not built, and a security audit and mainnet trial come before real money.

## Contract work

- The author of Reins takes contract work and is available now:
  https://r2rlabs.com/build/ — contact hello@r2rlabs.com
- Built most often: MCP servers for an existing API, exchange and trading
  integrations, and guardrails that hold outside the model.
- Other kinds of project are considered too. Scope decides, not category.
- Fixed price against a fixed scope, agreed in writing before work starts. The
  client owns the repository, the licence and the accounts.
- Scoping happens by email rather than by call, so the scope and the price are
  documented.
- Reins itself is the worked example: shipped to npm, PyPI and the MCP registry,
  445 tests, verified against a funded mainnet account, with the losing demo run
  published rather than buried.

## Not

- Not an exchange, not a broker, not a fund. It holds no customer funds.
- Not a trading strategy: it does not decide what to trade, only what is allowed.
- Nothing on this site is financial advice.
